items.title: ASX falls as banks, tech stocks decline; CSL names new chair
paras: The S&P/ASX 200 was down 64.9 points or 0.7 per cent, to 8730.3 in early trade. Wall Street lost ground on Friday as oil prices hit their highest mark in four years.

Bloomberg Financial stocks are weaker across the board, with Commonwealth Bank leading the way for the big four banks with a 2 per cent decline. National Australia Bank lost 1.7 per cent while Westpac and ANZ Bank each shed 1.9 per cent.

Energy stocks advanced after oil prices rose again over the weekend before easing this morning as the US and Iran remained apart on a deal to end months of war. President Donald Trump told Fox News it was “getting to be decision time” on whether he would make a deal with Tehran or “finish it off”.

items.title: India, Rotterdam port authorities engaged to digitalise cargo processes: Piyush Goyal
paras: Rotterdam, Oct 25 (PTI) Indian and Rotterdam port authorities are working to digitalise processes in India to speed up cargo evacuation and reduce ship turnaround times, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday. He said that there is a need to significantly improve the port capacity in India.
The minister visited the Port of Rotterdam and met Port of Rotterdam CEO Boudewijn Siemons. “Despite doubling our port capacity over the past decade, India still needs more capacity.

By 2047, we expect port capacity to double twice over the next two decades to support GDP growth and international trade,” he said. He added that the India -EU Free Trade Agreement will provide huge potential to businesses of both sides. Rotterdam port is Europe’s largest port, serving as a gateway for Indian goods to the European market and a key hub for international trade and global supply chains.

items.title: German firms see India as manufacturing, R&D & innovation hub: Goyal
paras: Berlin, Oct 24 (PTI) German companies are increasingly viewing India as a strategic hub for manufacturing, research and development, and innovation alongside its role as a key consumer market, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said.

Addressing the media after concluding his two-day visit here, the minister said he held a series of bilateral meetings with representatives from companies including Siemens Healthcare, Bertelsmann Investment, Volkswagen and Skoda.

“The CEOs echoed one message – German companies no longer see India only as a market, but as their partner, as a base for manufacturing, for research and development, for innovation,” he said. German precision and research, combined with India’s skill and talent to innovate and manufacture for the future, and investing in the India growth story, will change the global perspective and outlook toward India, he said.

items.title: Australia’s $1.4 Trillion Question: How Much of the national Super balance was built by taxpayers?
paras: Our recent articles questioning Australia’s superannuation system have focused on a simple proposition: a system controlling nearly $5 trillion of Australians’ wealth deserves considerably more scrutiny than it receives. We have examined ten reasons the existing compulsory superannuation model should be looked at.

We have also proposed a parallel alternative — a government-backed Digital Pension Scheme (DPS) — designed to provide retirement security without requiring every additional dollar of compulsory retirement saving to pass through private funds management. How much of Australia’s enormous superannuation pool was actually created by government tax concessions?

Our modelling suggests that around $1.4 trillion of Australia’s superannuation assets at June 2026 can potentially be attributed to accumulated Commonwealth tax concessions and the investment returns generated by those concessions. That is approximately 30% of the entire Australian superannuation system .

items.title: India-New Zealand FTA: Over 50% of Indian exports already faced zero standard tariffs before deal
paras: New Delhi: The Free Trade Agreement (FTA) between India and New Zealand, which came into force on 20 October, promises greater market access for exporters in both countries. But, trade data for 2025 shows that India already had a trade surplus with New Zealand, and that its exports faced substantially lower standard tariff rates than New Zealand’s goods entering India.

India’s largest export categories to New Zealand, fuels and chemicals, also largely fell under zero-tariff categories before the FTA came into force . As a result, tariff reductions could matter more for Indian exporters of textiles, machinery and metals.

For New Zealand, wood and paper products qualify for immediate duty elimination, while vegetable products, chemicals and base metals will largely receive phased or conditional concessions. Pre-FTA tariff structures In 2025, India exported goods worth $881.75 million to New Zealand, while New Zealand exported $575.64 million worth of goods to India, according to international trade data.

items.title: October 26, 2006: The day Mary Pierce’s career was brought to an end by a horrifying injury
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back in time to one of the key moments in tennis history. On this day in 2006, Mary Pierce was taken off the court on a stretcher and would never return to compete on the Tour again

On this day, October 26, 2006, Mary Pierce suffered a horrifying injury while facing Vera Zvonareva in the second round of the WTA Linz Open. The two-time Grand Slam champion tore several knee ligaments, an injury that put an end to her career as she was never able to play on the professional circuit again.

Mary Pierce was born in 1975 in Montreal, Canada, but holding French citizenship from her mother, she chose to play for France. Pierce’s early career was impacted by her father’s violent behaviour, which in 1993 led the WTA to ban him from attending any tournament.
items.impact: After claiming four other tournaments in the next two years and reaching the quarter-finals at the 1993 Australian Open , she reached the final at Roland-Garros in 1994.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
